scope: Session 503 stabilization and forms/cases activity hubs

localFixes: Server anon Auth clients now use the complete-response deadline already used by browser and middleware; scoped deadlines retain Request and caller cancellation.
Case cookie authentication now classifies provider/network timeouts as CASE_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE (503), preserving 401 only for missing or definitively rejected sessions.
Viewer permission checks preserve temporary Auth failures as 503 instead of incorrectly reporting invalid credentials.
Case option catalogs load in one parallel wave after identity, case access, membership and subject scope are established; document ownership and signature compatibility filters remain enforced.
secondReview.liveDatabaseMaintenance: ANALYZE cron.job_run_details; updated stale planner statistics only. No cron disabled, history deleted, grants changed or paid resources added.
secondReview.cronFinding: The health query scans approximately 82,800 history rows. Only runid is indexed. The managed table belongs to supabase_admin; no ownership change or privilege escalation attempted. ANALYZE improved the row estimates but did not demonstrate a latency improvement (separate samples about 4 and 10 seconds).
secondReview.backgroundJobs: System task rules and open tasks still exist, so the workers were retained. Cumulative pg_stat_statements figures since October 15 are historical totals, not current per-minute load.

providerWindow.scope: One aggregate query, no tokens, emails, IPs or raw errors retained
providerWindow.caveat: Provider-recorded responses do not include proof that every client received a complete response before its deadline. Local 503s remain part of the incident evidence.
